title: Large Language Modelsfor Injury Surveillance: Evidence from E-Bike Incidents
abstract: arXiv:2506.04654v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This study analyzes e-bike-related injury incidents using two complementary data sources: the Consumer Product Safety Risk Management System (CPSRMS) and the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS). We develop an LLM-assisted framework that converts unstructured incident narratives into structured variables, notably human-, equipment-, and environment-related contributing factors, for use alongside demographic, locational, temporal, and weather-derived predictors. To improve cross-source comparability, injury severity is harmonized into three ordered categories. Separate ordered logit models are estimated for CPSRMS and NEISS, together with two supplementary joint scaled specifications. translated_title: 大语言模型用于伤害监测：来自电动自行车事故的证据
translated_abstract: 本研究利用两个互补的数据源分析电动自行车相关的伤害事故：消费者产品安全风险管理系统（CPSRMS）和国家电子伤害监测系统（NEISS）。我们开发了一个大语言模型辅助的框架，将非结构化的事故叙述转换为结构化变量，特别是与人、设备和环境相关的促成因素，以便与人口统计、位置、时间及天气衍生预测变量共同使用。为提高跨数据源的可比性，伤害严重程度被统一划分为三个有序类别。研究分别为CPSRMS和NEISS估计了独立的有序logit模型，并加入了两个补充性的联合尺度设定。在CPSRMS中，与人相关的因素与更高的伤害严重程度相关，而设备、环境相关因素、18岁以下骑手、春季事故以及娱乐/运动场所则与较低的严重程度相关。
tldr: 该研究开发了一个大语言模型辅助框架，将电动自行车事故的非结构化叙述转换为结构化的促成因素，并利用有序logit模型发现人为因素与更高的伤害严重程度相关，而设备、环境因素、年轻骑手及娱乐运动场所则与较低严重程度相关。
en_tdlr: This study develops an LLM-assisted framework that converts unstructured e-bike incident narratives into structured contributing factors, and uses ordered logit models to show that human-related factors are associated with higher injury severity, while equipment/environment factors, riders under 18, and recreational locations are associated with lower severity.
